newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases marginally, market quiet.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases marginally, market quiet.

text.p: German call money eased slightly on Wednesday to around 3.05/07 percent from 3.07/08 percent on Tuesday, helped by the addition of 1.3 billion marks in this week's repo tender.
But dealers said, with an eye on reserve levels, that they believed call money rates were unlikely to fall much further.
"Reserve levels are not exactly generous," one trader said.
Banks held 38.6 billion marks of reserves at the central bank on Tuesday for an average of 40.8 billion for the month to July 8. Lombard borrowing was negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was calculated at 3.08692 percent, down from 3.10000 on Tuesday.
